subject: Data disposition & residency — Hosted API questionnaire
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API — data residency & disposition questions (Glomerate)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. To move this through our procurement/security review I need written answers for a short set of questions about Redwood's hosted API handling of customer data. Please provide short, precise answers we can include in our RFP. Key items we need:

1) Where is customer content (request/response payloads, logs) stored geographically for the hosted API? Can this be restricted to a single region (US-EAST, EU) for our account?
2) Default retention for request/response logs and diagnostic traces; can retention be shortened by contract (e.g., 7 days)?
3) Deletion guarantees: when a customer requests deletion, how quickly is data removed from primary storage and from backups/snapshots? What are the SLAs for purge propagation?
4) Backups and disaster recovery: are backups encrypted separately? What is the maximum backup retention period?
5) Encryption and key management: do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for hosted API stored data?
6) Process for verification/audit: what artifacts can you provide (logs, deletion receipts) to confirm a deletion request was completed?

If you can attach a short statement or diagram that we can attach to our questionnaire, that would be great.

Looking to get this back by EOD Thursday (US PST) if possible.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Security Operations
Glomerate Inc.

[Attachment requested: Section B of Glomerate security questionnaire]

Subject: Re: Hosted API — data residency & disposition questions (Glomerate)

Elena,

Thanks — attaching a consolidated statement for your questionnaire and answering inline below. Neha and Marissa are looped in to confirm technical details and add any contractual options.

On Mon, Feb 20, 2028 at 9:12 AM Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com> wrote:
> 1) Where is customer content ... Can this be restricted to a single region?

Answer: Customer request/response payloads and associated operational logs for the hosted API are stored in the cloud region selected at account creation (we support US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST, and APAC regions). For enterprise customers we support region-locking so data is kept and processed only within the selected region.

> 2) Default retention for logs; can retention be shortened?

Answer: Default retention for request/response logs and diagnostic traces is 30 days. For enterprise contracts we can reduce retention to 7 days or implement a configurable retention policy as part of the account profile.

> 3) Deletion guarantees and propagation to backups?

Answer: Deletion requests initiated via the Console or Support ticket remove data from active primary storage within 72 hours. Purge from immutable backups and snapshots is propagated within 14 days; we provide a deletion confirmation once propagation completes. For customers requiring accelerated purges we offer contractual SLAs and additional deletion workflows.

> 4) Backups and DR retention?

Answer: Backups are encrypted and retained up to 60 days by default. Longer retention can be negotiated; disaster recovery snapshots are stored in the same region unless cross-region DR is requested and contractually agreed.

> 5) Encryption / KMS?

Answer: All data at rest is encrypted (AES-256); in transit uses TLS 1.3. We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM-backed KMS is available for enterprise plans.

> 6) Verification / audit artifacts?

Answer: We provide deletion receipts, per-request audit logs, and exportable activity logs for the retention/deletion events. SOC 2-type evidence and sample deletion receipts are in the attached statement.

Attaching: redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf — this is a short, non-engineering summary suitable for RFPs.

Subject: Re: Hosted API — data residency & disposition questions (internal clarification)

Quick clarifications / proposed wording tweaks for the statement (technical team sign-off):

- Region locking: confirm that metadata and control-plane records (account config, billing) are stored in our control plane (US by default) but request/response payloads and logs are pinned to the customer-selected data region. We'll add a single sentence clarifying control-plane vs data-plane separation.

- Retention: 30 days default for request/response logs is correct. For debugging we keep high-fidelity diagnostic traces for up to 90 days but those are strictly access-controlled and only accessible by SRE with JIT approval; we should not surface that to customers unless requested.

- Deletion propagation: primary-delete within 72 hours; snapshots/backups propagation target 14 days. Note: immutable backups (for legal/incident hold) may extend beyond 14 days — if customer requires true legal hold removal that needs an explicit contract clause.

- Backups: encrypted with envelope encryption; separate KMS key per customer is available on enterprise plan.

- Audit artifacts: we can provide a deletion receipt that includes deletion ticket id, timestamp of primary purge, and timestamp of backup purge propagation. Include example in the attached PDF.

I updated the attached PDF with the wording above and added the redwood-secure link to our internal disposition page for evidence.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Hosted API — data disposition & residency questions (final responses)

Elena — attaching a Glomerate-ready PDF (Section B) with the final answers (see attachment). Key points we've consolidated below for quick paste into your RFP: 

• Data residency: Customer data (request/response payloads, logs) is stored in the customer-selected region. Region-lock (single-region processing and storage) is supported for enterprise accounts. Control-plane metadata may remain in our control plane.

• Retention: Default request/response and diagnostic log retention is 30 days. Enterprise retention can be shortened to 7 days or set to a custom policy by contract. High-fidelity traces retained up to 90 days are only accessible to SRE under JIT approvals and will not be included in standard exports.

• Deletion: We purge primary storage within 72 hours and propagate deletion to backups/snapshots within 14 days. We will provide a deletion confirmation that includes ticket id and timestamps. Accelerated purge SLAs can be included in the contract if needed.

• Backups & DR: Backups are encrypted, envelope-encryption with per-customer keys available on enterprise plans. Default backup retention is 60 days; cross-region DR is optional and contractual.

• Encryption & KMS: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit. Redwood-managed keys by default; customer-managed cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys available for enterprise.

• Audit & verification: We provide deletion receipts, exportable audit logs, and sample artifacts. SOC 2 report excerpts are available under NDA.

Attached: Glomerate-Security-Responses-SectionB.pdf (filled-in answers) and the public redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf.
